ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
In the circuit shown in Figure A, the primary coil of the ideal transformer has 220 turns, and the number of turns in the secondary coil is adjustable. $L_{1}$, $L_{2}$, $L_{3}$, and $L_{4}$ are four identical light bulbs. When an alternating voltage as shown in Figure B is applied across terminals $M$ and $N$, the number of turns in the secondary coil is adjusted so that all four bulbs light up normally.

1. The voltage across the primary coil of the transformer
2. The maximum rate of change of magnetic flux through the primary coil of the transformer

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: In the circuit shown in Figure A, the primary coil of the ideal transformer has 220 turns, and the number of turns in the secondary coil is adjustable. L1, L2, L3, and L4 are four identical light bulbs. When an alternating voltage as shown in Figure B is applied across terminals M and N, the number of turns in the secondary coil is adjusted so that all four bulbs light up normally. 1. The voltage across the primary coil of the transformer 2. The maximum rate of change of magnetic flux through the primary coil of the transformer
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The left side of Figure A is the circuit connected across the two terminals M and N; bulb L1 is in the upper branch, L2 is in the lower branch, and the primary coil n1 of the transformer is in the right branch, so L1, the primary coil, and L2 are in series; on the right side of Figure A, the secondary coil n2 and bulbs L3 and L4 form a series closed circuit. Figure B is a sinusoidal graph of the AC voltage u between M and N varying with time, with the peak value marked as 220√2 V and the negative peak value as -220√2 V. Reasoning: The peak value given in Figure B is 220√2 V, so the effective value of the voltage between M and N is U_MN=220 V. Let the effective voltage when each identical bulb emits light normally be U_b, the normal current be I_b, and the normal power be P_b=U_b I_b. On the secondary side, L3 and L4 both emit light normally, and the total power is 2P_b; an ideal transformer has no loss, so the input power on the primary side is also 2P_b. The primary coil is in series with L1 and L2, and L1 and L2 emit light normally, so the effective value of the primary-side current is equal to the normal current I_b of the bulbs. Therefore the effective voltage across the primary coil is U1=P_primary/I_b=2P_b/I_b=2U_b. In the primary-side circuit, L1 and L2 together drop voltage 2U_b, and the primary coil is also 2U_b, so the total effective voltage is 4U_b=220 V, obtaining U_b=55 V, therefore the primary coil voltage U1=110 V. The peak value of the primary coil voltage is 110√2 V. From the instantaneous value of the induced voltage of the primary coil of an ideal transformer satisfying |u1|=N1 |dΦ/dt|, and N1=220 turns, the maximum magnetic flux change rate is (110√2)/220=0.5√2 Wb/s.
